description: The central gateway's route ids, published as data so a consumer does not keep its own copy. Owned here, where the routes are defined. 'delegate_rows_may_name' is the published answer to whether a delegate row may name a route: read that field rather than deciding it from the route's name, its module, or a list kept elsewhere.

routes.note: The delegate table is keyed on this route. A delegate row naming it authorizes reads and says nothing about any other route.

The listing of assets a caller may read. ITS OWN id, not a reuse of assets.authorize: the delegate table is keyed per route, so sharing an id would widen every row granted for reads to a route nobody granted. The consequence is a policy fact, not a code one -- a service listed as a delegate for assets.authorize alone is refused not_a_delegate here until a row names this id too. A listing is the weaker operation, which is what makes inferring the grant tempting; the table cannot express weaker, so inferring it would make its rows mean something other than what they say.
An internal door. It authorizes against its own caller list and never consults the delegate table.
